summary: Feed c033_link_crc to SIEM is degraded: NPB-01 port 1/1 shows high CRC/alignment errors (0.486%) and 1.45% packet loss between DC-CORE-1 SPAN destination and NPB input. Both indicate Layer 1 fault on the link into the packet broker causing corrupted and missing traffic before the SIEM.

findings.root_cause: Physical layer fault on NPB-01 port 1/1 (input) - 19,860 damaged frames with CRC/alignment errors (0.486% vs 0.001% threshold). Most likely faulty cable, bad optic, or duplex mismatch on the link into the broker corrupting frames on the wire.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM receives corrupted frames that are dropped by NIC/broker and never logged. Even though SIEM does not need full payload, FCS failures mean events are lost entirely, creating detection gaps and incomplete correlation.

recommended_fix.why: No broker policy can recover frames already corrupted at ingress. Fix/replace cable/optic, check duplex/speed negotiation and error counters on both ends to eliminate CRC errors before forwarding to SIEM.

findings.root_cause: Loss on the link between DC-CORE-1 Gi1/0/48 (SPAN destination) and NPB-01 port 1/1 - SPAN sent 4,146,420 packets but broker saw only 4,086,300 (60,120 lost, 1.45% vs 0.1% threshold). Same faulty cable/optic, dirty fiber, or unmonitored patch causing drops between SPAN output and broker input.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM is blind to ~1.45% of SPAN traffic at random. Missing packets hide alerts, break flow/session reconstruction and reduce detection coverage for lateral movement and exfiltration.

recommended_fix.why: Restore lossless delivery from SPAN destination to broker. Reseat/replace cable/optic, verify SPAN destination not oversubscribed/dropping, and if loss persists consider replacing SPAN with TAP for reliable capture.
